name: @aztec-avm-runtime/orchestration
description: Aztec's own public transaction orchestration, over the wasm AVM
//: WHAT IS AND IS NOT IN THIS PACKAGE. Corrected in M18's review because the first version of
this note said the opposite, and CORRECTED AGAIN IN M22 because it then went stale in the
other direction: it said the block processor was NOT vendored here, and now it is.
VENDORED HERE, under src/vendor/, from the `ts` anchor and registered in PROVENANCE.md
(F10..F19) so `just check-drift` compares every one of them against that commit on every run:
upstream's `PublicProcessor` and `GuardedMerkleTreeOperations` and its metrics (RI-21),
`public_db_sources.ts` + `contracts_db_checkpoint.ts` + `db_interfaces.ts` (RI-23),
`side_effect_errors.ts` + `public_errors.ts` (RI-22), `PublicTxSimulatorInterface` (RI-19),
and TXE's block-creation helpers (RI-66). Ten files, five of them byte-identical to upstream.
STILL NOT VENDORED, and still an outstanding task: the three-phase transaction model in
`public_tx_simulator/` (RI-19 — only its INTERFACE came across, because the processor takes
its simulator as a constructor argument and `WasmAvmPublicTxSimulator` satisfies it), the
state manager (RI-20) and the side-effect trace (RI-22, due in M25).
@aztec/simulator is STILL NOT a dependency, and the reason is unchanged and is NOT that
upstream does not publish it — IT DOES, at the exact nightly tag this package already pins,
exporting './server'. The reason is that `npm view @aztec/simulator@<pin> dependencies` lists
`@aztec/native` and `@aztec/world-state` as HARD dependencies, so importing it would pull the
NAPI AVM and the LMDB world-state addon into the shipped tree — which DD-9 forbids and which
`verify_differential_containment` asserts against, in three places. Vendoring from the pinned
anchor is what gets the code without the dependency edge.
NO `PublicProcessorFactory`. The vendored processor drops it, because its `protected
createPublicTxSimulator` hard-defaults to `TelemetryCppPublicTxSimulator` — the NAPI AVM —
with no flag. `PublicProcessor`'s own constructor takes the simulator as its fourth positional
argument, so injection replaces inheritance and nothing else about the class moves.
WHAT IS HERE IS UPSTREAM'S. The msgpack encoder for the AVM's own input schema is — it is
`serializeWithMessagePack` in @aztec/stdlib/avm, which is what CppPublicTxSimulator calls
on exactly this type. What is ours is the transport: where CppPublicTxSimulator hands the
encoded blob to @aztec/native's `avmSimulate`, WasmAvmPublicTxSimulator hands it to
avm.wasm through @aztec-avm-runtime/node-host. M22 adds two more of ours, and both are
adapters rather than reimplementations: `ResidentMerkleWriteOperations` (RI-67) and
`ResidentContractsDB` (RI-68), between upstream's interfaces and the module's exports.
@aztec/telemetry-client is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the dependency list. It is replaced
by src/telemetry.ts, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: see that file.
@aztec/native and @aztec/world-state are DELIBERATELY ABSENT too. The first is the C++
AVM over NAPI, which DD-9 says no public export of ours may reach; the second is an
LMDB-backed native addon, replaced by Aztec's own world_state_reference compiled into
avm.wasm (RI-27). ForkCheckpoint, the one production import that package supplied to this
subtree, is copied into src/fork_checkpoint.ts.
